title: Nomic C Rules Specification
description: Complete specification for writing Nomic C compliance checker rules. This document comprehensively describes all features, capabilities, and DSL functions available for rule authoring.

rule_structure.description: Complete YAML structure for defining a Nomic rule

id.description: Unique identifier for the rule (e.g., SEC-001, MEMSAFE-010, QUALITY-020)

description.description: Human-readable description of what the rule checks
examples: Format string vulnerability - user data in format string
Potential buffer overflow in fixed-size buffer operations

meanings.error: Critical issues that must be fixed
meanings.warning: Important issues that should be addressed

scope.description: What type of entity this rule applies to

select.description: DSL expression to select entities to check

where.description: Optional filter to narrow down selected entities before assertion
where.purpose: Pre-filter entities to improve performance and clarity

assert.description: Boolean expression that must be true to pass the rule
assert.note: If this evaluates to false, a violation is reported
examples: forall p in parameters, not isPointer(p) or hasNullCheck(p)

message.description: Message shown when rule is violated. Can use {placeholders} for entity properties
examples: Function {name} has cyclomatic complexity of {cyclomaticComplexity}. Consider refactoring (threshold: 10).
Function {name} does not check malloc return value. Always check for NULL.
Variable {name} is not initialized. Initialize variables at declaration.

fixit.description: Optional suggested fix for the violation

exceptions.description: Patterns for entities that should be excluded from this rule

dsl_language.description: Nomic's Domain-Specific Language (DSL) for writing rule expressions

membership.in: Check if element is in collection

forall.description: True if CONDITION is true for ALL elements
examples: forall p in parameters, not isPointer(p) or isConst(p)

exists.description: True if CONDITION is true for AT LEAST ONE element
examples: exists v in local_variables, not isInitialized(v)

none.description: True if CONDITION is true for NO elements
examples: none p in parameters, isPointer(p) and not isConst(p)

best_practices.description: Best practices for writing effective rules
rule_design: Use specific rule IDs with category prefixes (SEC-, MEMSAFE-, QUALITY-)
Write clear, actionable messages with context
Include relevant CWE numbers for security rules
Use appropriate severity levels (error for critical, warning for important, info for suggestions)
Add comprehensive tags for filtering and categorization
performance: Use where clause to pre-filter entities before expensive assertions
Prefer built-in functions over complex DSL expressions
Avoid redundant checks in both where and assert
maintainability: Document complex DSL expressions with comments in YAML
accuracy: Minimize false positives with precise conditions
Use exceptions list for known good patterns

check_all_parameters.example: forall p in parameters, not isPointer(p) or isConst(p)

possible_causes: where clause is too restrictive and filters out all entities
Entity not being analyzed (check select expression)
solutions: Test where clause separately to verify it matches entities
Simplify assert to verify it can be false
Verify scope matches (function for functions, variable for variables)
Check that select expression returns entities
Add more specific conditions to where clause
Use exceptions list to exclude known patterns
Refine assert to be more precise
Consider using exists instead of forall for quantifiers
Use == for comparison, = is not valid
Verify function names in builtin_functions list
